title: The wave paid run of e905742 is red in 9 eval cases
what: Find why 39 code graders and 14 meaning graders failed in the paid run of master e905742, name the cause per group (a case set up wrong, a grader reading the old sdd plugin name, a real behaviour regression), fix it, and prove it with a paid run of only the failing cases.
why: 25 Oct, the wave paid run after the night's merges (OpenSpec optional, quick-head, rules-gate, train-2, it-terms, train-4): bin/ci RED, plugin evals FAILED (4196 s, $15.03). Every no-spec-step run failed even its "no-openspec-command" grader, which points at the case set-up or the grader, not at the model. relay sync waits for a green run. IP chosen by the front (agent-chosen): a red run is one fix item at the top.
failing_case: scratchpad ci-wave-e905742.log: "ci: eval record: NOT A PASS: 14 meaning grader(s) failed, 39 code grader(s) failed, 1 not judged, in code-reviewer-offbyone, it-terms-es, it-terms-ru, no-spec-step, no-spec-step-ru, no-spec-step-typo, spec-step-on, spec-step-on-ru, tune-no-price".
pass_cases: A paid run of the nine cases on the fix branch passes, and the cause of each group is named with evidence from the run's transcripts.
where: evals/plugin (it-terms-ru, it-terms-es, no-spec-step*, spec-step-on*, code-reviewer-offbyone, tune-no-price)
plugins/openspec the eval runner and its code graders

fact: Migration 27 Oct: the link in `failing_case` line 1 points to a session file (`ci-wave-e905742.log` and `reports/wave-red.md`), which is deleted when the machine restarts; the facts it held that this item rests on are the notes below.

Causes found 27 Oct for the red paid run of e905742 (wave-red report): (1) no-spec-step, -ru, -typo: a grader fault (it matched the word openspec in any Bash input, e.g. `find .claude openspec docs`) and a real behaviour (in 3 of 3 reproduced runs the session loaded the skill openspec:plan in a project with an openspec/ folder and no [specs] setting; fixed in the skill descriptions); (2) code-reviewer-offbyone: a set-up fault (the reviewer rule was committed on a branch only, so the hook that hands it to the critic never saw it on master); (3) it-terms-es, it-terms-ru: the eval runner does not load the scaffold's CLAUDE.md (a probe case asking for the words BANANA, CHERRY, MANGO in the reply got none of them in 3 runs, cost $0.04), so the rule never reached the model; (4) spec-step-on, -ru, -en, -typo: a meaning grader judged the order of tool calls from the last message only; (5) tune-no-price: "1 of 3 runs missing, not judged": the run hit its money ceiling ($15.03 of $15) before the last case ran. Final paid run after the fixes: one run of each failing case, 3 runs per case, $9.62; it-terms-ru remained flaky (model behaviour).
